touches.text: First class object (not a device): a thing with a charter that is not a rung of its own (Rescue, Graph Trees, Ticket).

The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else (Akien, 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02).
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor).
Shareable provenance (charters, tickets, validations) is git JSON beside the code, never a row.
It keeps the register of every ticket: open, at sea, in port. Task, trouble and fixit tickets show there too; inference tickets do not.
TESTER MACHINE, CodeMother's (was the tester device, cairn/devices/tester/)
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

A sieve's rule follows the ticket's kind (Akien, 2026-10-31: "for new/changed code tickets the rule is x, for fixit tickets the rule is y"). It is read off the ticket, so it stays deterministic, and 19.14.7 is left for what x and y do not cover.

y, fixit (bug): at BUILDME the ticket names the red it fixes (the proof), and that proof really is red on disk now; the named proof may be red, fixing it is the job. The fix may change the test case itself without a ruling: the proof's why names the ticket and says what it tests and why it changed, and names any tooth it removed. At PROVED it is sealed green and hollow-measured, as x.

A ticket cannot call itself a fixit to get y: y needs a real red on disk, which code checks. The harbor's proven-space rule (10.8) and the tester's rung 4 (11) each apply x or y by the ticket's kind; rung 4 no longer asks who answered.
post_commit: the one git post-commit, fanned out to each component's own hook. A commit is an event. → Recovery? (a host-seam) [Q#60]
